rows.subtopic: Fundamental Concepts in Organic Reaction Mechanism
rows.text:
Arrange the following compounds in order of decreasing basicity.

(i) 4,5-dihydro-1H-imidazole

(ii) pyrrole

(iii) imidazole

(iv) pyridine

figure.note: Four ring structures labelled (i)-(iv): (i) five-membered ring with N and NH, one C=N double bond and a CH2-CH2 edge (2-imidazoline); (ii) pyrrole with N-H at the bottom; (iii) imidazole, N and NH; (iv) pyridine.

rows._flag: The four compounds are drawn as structures only; their names are typed into the stem from the drawing.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
rows.text:
In the following reaction sequence, predict the structure of the final product **Y**.

\(\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_2COOCH_3} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{HCl\ gas}]{\mathrm{HOCH_2CH_2OH}} \mathbf{X} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{1.\ LiAlH_4;\ 2.\ H_2O}} \mathbf{Y}\)

figure.note: Scheme: H5C6-C(=O)-CH2-C(=O)-OCH3 --[HO-CH2CH2-OH above the arrow, 'HCl gas' below]--> X --[1. LiAlH4, 2. H2O]--> Y.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
rows.text:
For the following reaction, identify the carbonyl compound **X** that shows the highest reactivity.

\(\mathbf{X} + \mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2NH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+\ (anhydrous)}}\) Imine product
rows._flag: The amine is drawn as a skeletal propyl chain ending in NH2 and is typed as CH3CH2CH2NH2.

How many nodes are there in the antibonding molecular orbital formed by two \(2s\) atomic orbitals?

Identify the major product in the following reaction

2-phenylcyclohexan-1-one \(\xrightarrow[\mathrm{ii.\ H_2O}]{\mathrm{i.\ CH_3CH_2MgBr}} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2SO_4\ (conc.),\ reflux}} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{ii.\ Zn,\ H_2O}]{\mathrm{i.\ O_3}}\) ?

figure.note: Scheme: cyclohexanone with C6H5 on the carbon next to C=O --[i. CH3CH2MgBr, ii. H2O]--> --[H2SO4 (conc.), reflux]--> --[i. O3, ii. Zn, H2O]--> ?

rows._flag: The starting ketone is drawn; its name is typed into the stem. Option chains were counted from a 400 dpi render (B and D: three CH2 between CHO and the CH; C: four CH2 between the two C=O).

rows.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
rows.text: Which of the following complexes is expected to be colored?
Density of 3M solution of NaCl is 1.25 \(g/mL\). Calculate the volume of water required to make 1000 \(mL\) of this NaCl solution. [Consider the density of water as 1 \(g/mL\)].

Electric current was passed through an aqueous solution of \(\mathrm{CuSO_4}\) using two Pt electrodes. After some time, the blue color of the solution disappeared along with evolution of \(\mathrm{O_2}\) gas. Which of the following statements is correct regarding the resultant solution?

Reactant \(R\) gives \(n\) different products (\(P_r : r = 1, 2, 3, \cdots, n\)) in \(n\) parallel first order reactions. Rate constant for the formation of any product \(P_r\) is \(rk\) where \(r = 1, 2, 3, \cdots, n\). For the decay of \(R\), what is the overall rate constant in terms of \(k\)?

Consider a hypothetical case in which the charge of a proton is twice as that of an electron. Using this hypothetical case, how many protons (P), neutrons (N) and electrons (E) would a neutral \(\mathrm{^{23}Na}\) atom contain?

The magnitude of reversible work done by an ideal gas in four different processes: isothermal expansion, adiabatic expansion, constant pressure expansion, and free expansion are \(W_i\), \(W_a\), \(W_p\), and \(W_f\) respectively. Choose the right order of sequence for the magnitude of the work done. (Change in the volume is same for all the processes.)
